title: The gap from the response summary

blocks.text: A depot-siting team archives the end of every CP-SAT log. The last block starts with the line `CpSolverResponse summary:` and holds one `key: value` line per field (`status`, `objective`, `best_bound`, `branches`, ...), up to the end of the log.

items: `read_summary(log)`: a dict from each key in that block to its value, both as strings.
`relative_gap(log)`: the relative gap of the run, as the CP-SAT parameters proto defines it for `relative_gap_limit`, with $`O`$ the objective and $`B`$ the best bound:

blocks.text: The team solves both maximizations and minimizations. About twelve lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from summary import read_summary, relative_gap

# A made-up summary of a van-routing model, shaped like CP-SAT's.
log = ("#Done    0.80s main\n\nCpSolverResponse summary:\nstatus: FEASIBLE\nobjective: 1250\n"
       "best_bound: 1190\nbooleans: 44\nconflicts: 87\nbranches: 1502\nwalltime: 0.81\n")
fields = read_summary(log)
print("fields read:", fields)
print("gap at objective 1250, bound 1190:", round(relative_gap(log), 4))
print("gap at objective 0, bound 2:", relative_gap(log.replace("1250", "0").replace("1190", "2")))

cases.says: every line of the summary block becomes one key and its value
a stopped maximization's gap is the distance to the bound over the objective, and an optimal run's gap is 0
a minimization, whose bound is below its objective, has a positive gap
an objective of 0 divides by 1, not by 0

origin.section: The Response Summary Is the Run's Final Word

concepts: the response summary holds the final status, objective and bound, from which the gap follows
